pr_title: Teach tab tool tips to show key bindings
pr_body:
<!-- Please review the items on the PR checklist before submitting-->

* [x] CLA signed. 
* [ ] Tests added/passed
* [ ] Documentation updated. 
* [ ] Schema updated.
* [ ] I've discussed this with core contributors already. 

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments
Currently the tab tool tip is the tab's title.
The PR teaches the TabBase to check if there is a switch to tab command 
associated with the current tab index,
if so concatenates the the relevant mapping to the too tip.

Of course, prefers user defined bindings to the default ones.

Moved tool tip logic to TabBase so SettingsTab has tooltip as well.

![TabToolTip](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4639110/104823154-a1cb1100-5850-11eb-9dbd-bf23f5e6979d.gif)

# Description of the new feature/enhancement

It would be good to show a shortcut tooltip (`alt+1`, etc) when hovering on an unselected tab.

Users might know the shortcut only if they read Settings.

# Proposed technical implementation details (optional)

N/A
comments: This seems like a good and just idea. I think we already have code for creating a string from a ShortcutAction's key binding as well, so it shouldn't be that hard for someone to add a tooltip to the tab using that text.
A bit old I know, but can I work on this?
Sure! Feel free to take a crack at it.
I've been looking around for where the current tooltip is displayed (currently it's just the name of the tab) but I can't find it. Could I get some guidance on where that might be?

I thought it might be somewhere in the Tab.cpp, Tab.h, or TerminalPage files, but I couldn't find it. I did a search for "tooltip" that ended up bringing me mostly into autogenerated files which didn't seem to help much.

Honestly, we're not generating the tooltips for the TabViewItems currently. I'd bet that they're just being auto-generated by the TabViewItem template itself. Maybe you'll have luck looking in [here](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/tree/98a6b746dc409fa3c64bca4db2c3e6aa31e73470/dev/TabView)?
@ggadget6 - this has been stale for  a while, so I allowed myself to work on it.. if you have a solution we can absolutely discard mine.
@Don-Vito nope, that's fine. I had a partial solution but I got busy and wasn't able to finish it. You can go ahead with yours.

review_comments:
weird enough, I think we have another keychord->string converter too living in TerminalPage. Not sure which one we should use here. This one used to be used in settings re-serialization, so it was _less_ user-facing.

The one in TerminalApp is admittedly strange. Probably best not to use it.
